details: Renewed military actions, including US strikes against Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, have escalated Middle East tensions, contributing to a risk-off sentiment across global financial markets. This geopolitical uncertainty has led to a sell-off in technology stocks and dampened enthusiasm for risk assets, including Bitcoin, which has seen downward pressure.
title: US-Iran Tensions Impact Wall Street, Bitcoin Amid Risk-Off Mood

details: US consumer prices increased by 4.2% year-on-year in May, marking the largest gain since April 2023. This acceleration in inflation, partly due to higher energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict, is expected to reinforce the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance. Investors are now pricing in at least one 25-basis-point rate hike by year-end, which could create a less supportive environment for cryptocurrencies and other risk assets.
title: US Inflation Rises, Bolstering Fed Rate Hike Expectations

details: Spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) are experiencing continued significant net outflows, indicating weak institutional investor demand. This trend, with billions in withdrawals over recent weeks, suggests a cautious sentiment among large investors and contributes to the downward pressure on Bitcoin's price, reflecting a broader risk aversion in the market.
title: Persistent Bitcoin ETF Outflows Signal Weak Institutional Demand

details: Japan's three largest financial institutions – Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, and Mizuho Financial Group – plan to jointly issue stablecoins during the fiscal year ending March 2027. This initiative, involving the establishment of a collaborative council, represents a significant step towards integrating digital currencies into Japan's traditional financial system and could foster broader institutional adoption.
title: Japan's Top Banks to Jointly Issue Stablecoins by March 2027
